label: MORNING BRIEF

stories.title: Arcade basement shops must go
stories.story: Cabinet has ordered traders in parking basements turned into shops to leave immediately, after last year’s floods.
stories.you: Don’t let out basement shops. Those traders need space — list legal shops near town.

stories.title: Home loans at 16.9%
stories.story: dfcu now lends up to 85% of a finished home’s value, over up to 20 years. Ugandans abroad can apply.
stories.you: Buyers short of cash have options. Get them comparing bank home loans this week.

stories.title: Railway land is being cleared
stories.story: URC is clearing land within about 30 m (100 ft) of the line. Titles there will be cancelled, with no compensation.
stories.you: Plot near a railway? Check the reserve before you list it. A title is not enough.
stories.source: Sources: Nile Post, The Independent · Oct 2026

stories.title: Government is counting its land
stories.story: Councils had two weeks from 3 Nov to list all government land: where it is, who is on it, and its papers.
stories.you: Was the plot ever school, market or council land? Check its history before you list it.
stories.source: Sources: Nile Post, UG Standard · 3 Nov 2026

stories.title: Prices are climbing again
stories.story: Bank of Uganda expects inflation of 7.5–8% over the next year, up from 5.8% in October.
stories.you: Rents and building costs are likely to rise. Buyers who wait may pay more.
stories.source: Source: Bank of Uganda, via Nile Post · 9 Nov 2026
